# client-reporting-automation

Small Python toolkit for the repeatable parts of agency account coordination: client reports, scope and hours tracking, deadline flags, onboarding, QBR prep and meeting follow-through.

**All data is synthetic.** Clients, people, metrics, hours and meeting notes are generated by `cra/sample_data.py` with a fixed seed. Nothing here is real client data or a real result. Insights are plain threshold rules, not a model.

## Run

    python3 -m cra.sample_data          # regenerate data/ (already committed)
    python3 -m cra report --period weekly   # or monthly: HTML + markdown per client into out/
    python3 -m cra scope                # budget burn, overservicing alerts, utilization
    python3 -m cra status               # status board + at-risk deadline flags
    python3 -m cra onboard --client "Acme (fictional)" --date 2025-04-01 --channels search,email
    python3 -m cra qbr                  # QBR deck outline per client
    python3 -m cra notes data/meeting_notes.txt   # action items, decisions, risks
    python3 -m pytest

## What the rules do

- Reports: compares this period to the previous one (week vs week, 4 weeks vs 4 weeks). Wins at +10% conversions, -10% cost per conversion, +10% ROAS. Risks at -10% conversions, +15% cost per conversion, ROAS under 1, spend +15%.
- Scope: burn = hours used / monthly budget. "OVERSERVICING RISK" when burn runs 25% ahead of how far into the month we are; "OVER SCOPE" past 100%; "UNDERUSED" under half pace.
- Deadlines: OVERDUE, AT RISK (waiting on client within 3 days, or not started within 7), DUE SOON (2 days).
- Notes: picks up `Action:`, `TODO:`, `Next steps:` lines and "X will/to ..." phrases, finds owner and date when present, otherwise marks UNASSIGNED / no date.

Limits: the notes extractor is keyword-based and will miss loosely phrased tasks; thresholds are defaults to tune per client.
